prompt: The MS below shows M⁺ = 92 and a huge peak at m/z 91 (M−1). Which compound is it?

options.label: Toluene (M⁺ 92, loses benzylic H → aromatic tropylium at 91)
Aniline (M⁺ 93, loses H → 92; distinctive N-containing fragment)
Methylfuran (M⁺ 82, loses CHO → 53; m/z 91 wouldn't appear)

explanation: The famous m/z 91 TROPYLIUM cation (C₇H₇⁺) comes from benzylic H loss followed by ring expansion to the 7-membered aromatic tropylium. M⁺ 92 confirms toluene (C₇H₈). m/z 91 is a hallmark of any alkylbenzene. Benzene is M⁺ 78; aniline is 93, not 92.
